subject: Shopline trial: replan, new use case addendum, and owners
body:
From: jasmine_liu@redwood.com
To: Alex Martin <alex.martin@shopline.com>, Priya Rao <priya@shopline.com>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 12 Jan 2027 15:23:00 -0800
Subject: Shopline trial: post-call recap + proposed evaluation plan and owners

Hi Alex / Priya — thanks again for a productive call this morning. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have a shared plan for the 4-week trial. I’ve attached the draft evaluation workbook (POC-eval-plan-v1.xlsx).

Key success criteria (proposed)
- Latency: median token latency <= 150ms for search augmentation flows under test traffic.
- Accuracy: top-1 reranking improvement >= 15% on the sample queries in tab 'KPIs'.
- Cost: per-generated-response cost target <= $0.035 (model + infra) for the two high-throughput endpoints.
- Stability: 99.5% success rate (no server errors) over weekly runs.

Trial scope (week-by-week)
- Week 1: Environment setup, security review, baseline inference runs on 10k sample queries. Owners: Alex (Shopline) + Marissa (Redwood).
- Week 2: Run reranking experiments and fine-tune routing/prefix cache. Owners: Ben + Alex.
- Week 3: End-to-end integration (search + chat switch) and latency stress tests.
- Week 4: Quality review, handoff doc, and decision checkpoint (go/no-go).

Open items / asks for Shopline
- Please confirm 2-3 canonical evaluation queries and expected labels (drop into tab 'Queries').
- Provide access to a test S3 bucket or share sample payloads for integration by Friday.
- Security questionnaire (attached) — we need completed copy to start Private evals.

Next steps
- I’ll provision a sandbox Dedicated instance and share credentials by Thursday.
- Alex to send canonical queries and confirm point-of-contact for infra (Priya suggested).
- Ben and Marissa will prepare a short runbook for the Week 1 baseline.

Thanks — feel free to flag anything I missed.

Best,
Jasmine Liu
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
jasmine_liu@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0193

---

On Wed, 13 Jan 2027 09:02:00 -0500, Alex Martin <alex.martin@shopline.com> wrote:
> Hi Jasmine — great recap, appreciate the clarity. A couple notes from our side after syncing with product: we want to add a small extractive summarization use case to Weeks 2–3. Will that require a new acceptance metric?
> 
> Proposed addition:
> - Use case: Summaries for long-form product reviews to show on product pages.
> - Eval metric: ROUGE-L against gold summaries provided by our content team (sample set attached).
> 
> Impact: we expect this adds ~15% more inference volume and introduces multi-turn context handling for the same endpoints. We’re okay shifting timelines by a few days if needed.
> 
> I attached an updated set of sample queries (POC-eval-plan-v1.xlsx) with a new 'Summaries' tab and a quick security note.
> 
> Can Redwood scope this in without reworking pricing? If it looks like scope growth materially affects costs we’ll discuss separately but for now want to keep the trial intact.
> 
> -Alex
> Head of Product, Shopline


On Thu, 14 Jan 2027 10:11:00 -0800, ben_carter@redwood.com wrote:
> Jasmine / team — quick internal check: adding summarization means we should confirm two things before committing: 1) model variant that supports multi-turn summarization with acceptable tokenization+KV cache behavior; 2) capacity for the +15% volume during Week 3 stress tests.
> 
> I propose we do a short spike (1 day) on Jan 18 to validate latency/cost delta and report back. If that spike looks good, we fold summaries into the Week 2/3 plan and update the workbook.
> 
> Ben
> Product Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference


On Fri, 15 Jan 2027 09:12:00 -0800, jasmine_liu@redwood.com wrote:
> Thanks Ben — that sounds right. Alex / Priya: we’ll run Ben’s 1-day spike on Jan 18 (Ben + Marissa). If the spike shows latency <200ms median and cost delta <20% vs baseline, we’ll add the summarization use case to the official acceptance criteria and move the Week 3 stress window by two days.
> 
> Updated owners and timeline (final):
> - Jan 18: internal spike (Ben, Marissa).
> - Jan 19–20: Shopline provides final canonical summaries and sample payloads. (Owner: Alex)
> - Jan 21–27: integrated runs (includes summarization evaluations).
> - Jan 28: decision checkpoint and go/no-go; Redwood to provide runbook and cost delta summary.
> 
> Please confirm you’re aligned with the timeline and we’ll update the HubSpot deal with new milestone dates (link below). If Shopline prefers not to add summarization to the trial acceptance criteria, we can run it as an opt-in experiment but it won’t count toward the go/no-go decision.
> 
> HubSpot: https://app.hubspot.com/deals/4823/DEAL-2027-093
> Drive: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1aBcD-example-eval
> 
> Thanks — Jasmine
> 
> Jasmine Liu
> Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
> jasmine_liu@redwood.com
>
